purpose: Audit every profile without a Wikipedia object in the final iOS candidate catalog. Search status is separated from article suitability; absence from the catalog is not treated as proof that no article exists.

classificationDefinitions.candidate_article_found_identity_verifie: A read Wikipedia article/section explicitly identifies the assigned figure or a generic title identity; candidate link is reported, not inserted.
classificationDefinitions.candidate_page_found_identity_unconfirme: A relevant page exists and mentions the figure, but the article itself signals ambiguity, tradition, or a secondary identification that should not be made a direct identity claim.
classificationDefinitions.same_name_identity_unconfirmed: Relevant same-name page(s) were read, but they explicitly leave the assigned figure’s identity unresolved.
classificationDefinitions.no_appropriate_page_found: Targeted Wikipedia search was performed; no target-specific article was found or available pages were generic, unrelated, or chapter-level only.
classificationDefinitions.not_searched: No targeted Wikipedia search/read has yet been performed.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Alexander the Coppersmith
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article identifies the figure as the person named at 2 Timothy 4:14; says some scholars identify him with Acts 19:33 Alexander, while others distinguish them.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Acts 19:33 person cannot be identified with him conclusively.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Alexander (New Testament person)
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: New Testament-name disambiguation/list page; entries include high-priestly-family Alexander (Acts 4:6), an Ephesian Alexander and Alexander the Coppersmith; states the Ephesian figure could be the one at Acts 19:33.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Name-list page and expressly uncertain identification do not verify the assigned individual.

entries.recommendationJa: Search completed. No verified person-specific page for the Acts 19:33 Alexander. Do not merge with person:alexander_187 or Alexander the Coppersmith.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Crispus of Chalcedon
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: The article says Crispus was the Corinth synagogue ruler converted by Paul and cites Acts 18:8; also presents later bishop/saint tradition, with some cited claims marked citation needed.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Direct article candidate for Acts 18:8; preserve its later traditional biography as separate, unverified claims.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential article candidate; article directly names Acts 18:8 and matches the assigned Crispus.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Riot in Ephesus
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article describes the riot as set in motion by Demetrius the silversmith; its narrative quotes Acts 19:24–27 and says he made small silver shrines of Artemis.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Relevant shared/event article, not a standalone Demetrius biography.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential related/shared-section candidate; article’s Demetrius is the Acts 19:24 silversmith.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Gaius (biblical figure)
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Separate numbered entries explicitly describe a Macedonian Gaius traveling with Paul and Aristarchus (Acts 19:29), and a Gaius from Derbe one chapter later (Acts 20:4).
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Shared article discusses multiple same-name figures; use only a section/related link and keep the two catalog IDs distinct.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential related/shared-section candidate for the Macedonian Gaius. The page distinguishes Acts 19:29 from Acts 20:4.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Gaius (biblical figure)
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: A numbered entry identifies the Gaius with a residence in Derbe as a traveling companion in Acts 20:4; the preceding entry separately discusses Acts 19:29’s Macedonian Gaius.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Shared article discusses multiple same-name figures; do not conflate the two IDs.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential related/shared-section candidate for the Derbe Gaius, provided the link points to the Acts 20:4 entry.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Herod Antipas
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article identifies Antipas as a first-century tetrarch and covers his part in Jesus’s trial before Pilate. A separate Wikipedia “List of major biblical figures” page explicitly says Herod Antipas is called “Herod” in Acts 4:27.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Potential target mapping exists in a list page, but the assigned passage itself says only Herod and the current profile intentionally does not identify Antipas. Candidate requires editorial decision before linking.

entries.recommendationJa: A possible page exists, but the first-appearance profile leaves the individual unresolved. Do not attach without an explicit identity policy.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: James, brother of Jesus
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: The “Acts of the Apostles” section quotes Acts 12:17 and says the Catholic Encyclopedia identifies this James as James, brother of Jesus; it also connects him with the Jerusalem council and Acts 21:17–18.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Article makes a specific sourced identification, while Acts 12:17 alone does not provide the family link. Candidate for review; do not add a family relationship to the early profile on this basis alone.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential article candidate because it explicitly treats Acts 12:17’s James; identity is supported by a cited secondary identification, not the verse alone.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: New Testament people named John
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Dedicated subsection “John of the high-priestly family” quotes Acts 4:6, describes this John as mentioned once among the high-priest family, and discusses disputed identification with John the Apostle.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Exact shared-section fit; the article itself preserves the uncertainty and distinguishes him from other Johns.

entries.recommendationJa: Strong shared-section candidate; use this subsection and preserve its identity uncertainty.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Searches for Judah/Judas of Damascus and Acts 9:11
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Targeted searches did not surface a Wikipedia article for the householder in Acts 9:11. The evidence file identifies the WEB spelling Judah and notes KJV Judas; the passage identifies only the householder.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: No target-specific page found; common-name apostle articles would be different people.

entries.recommendationJa: Targeted search performed; no suitable page found. This is not a claim that no page can ever exist.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Titius Justus
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: German-language article identifies Titius Justus from Acts 18:7 as a God-fearer in Corinth and says Paul went to his house next to the synagogue.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Directly fits Acts 18:7. Targeted Japanese and English Wikipedia searches did not surface a suitable page; the German article is a candidate if non-Japanese language is acceptable.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential article candidate. Prefer Japanese if a suitable page is later found; otherwise this German article is specifically about the Acts 18:7 person.

entries.catalogNameJa: レバイオス（ヤコブの子ユダ）

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Jude the Apostle
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article’s opening calls him Judas son of James/Judas of James and lists Lebbaeus among names; its identity section cites Acts 1:13 and discusses disagreement about whether “of James” means son or brother and whether this Judas is Thaddeus.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Useful related candidate for the alternate-name question, but the article expressly reports contested harmonization; do not present the identification as certain.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential related-section candidate with explicit uncertainty. Stronger than “no suitable article”; preserve the draft’s caveat.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Lucius of Cyrene
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article quotes Acts 13:1 and identifies a Lucius of Cyrene in Antioch; however it headlines him as Lucius of Laodicea, also calls him Luke, and adds later episcopal/traditional identifications.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: A page exists and names the Acts figure, but conflation with Luke/Lucius of Laodicea and tradition makes a direct biography link unsafe without explicit related-link wording.

entries.recommendationJa: Candidate found, but not recommended as a direct identity link; the article conflates names and traditions.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Pharaoh
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article defines Pharaoh as the title/rule of ancient Egyptian monarchs; it does not identify the unspecified king in Acts 7:10 as a unique historical ruler.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Generic title article is not an individual match for this profile.

entries.recommendationJa: 日本語Wikipediaでも同定可能な一人の王の記事は確認できなかった。対象検索後も、一般的な称号記事はActs 7:10の王個人を特定しないため候補にしない。

entries.catalogNameJa: ファラオ（エジプト王の称号）

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Pharaoh
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article explicitly defines Pharaoh as the monarch/title of ancient Egypt and explains the title’s use; it does not identify a specific ruler.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Appropriate related-title explanation for the profile’s office-title identityType; not a biography or personal identification.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Pharaoh’s daughter (Exodus)
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: This is a different person—the daughter who adopts Moses. The article notes her father is unnamed.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Not a link for the Pharaoh title profile; avoid attaching daughter’s article to father/title.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential related article for the office-title profile only; it must not imply an individual king identity.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Saint Publius
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Article calls him Publius of Malta and says Acts describes Publius as “chief” of the island; it says Christian tradition identifies him as the Publius who received Paul after the shipwreck, and quotes Acts 28:7–10.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: Specific match candidate, but the biographical identification and later episcopal life are expressly tradition-based; use only as a related page and do not import those facts into the profile.

entries.recommendationJa: Potential related article. Newly found and read; older person_3 research only assessed a generic Publius page, so its “inadequate page” result does not evaluate this title.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Acts 20
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Existing person_3 research states the Acts 20 page’s verse 4 lists Secundus from Thessalonica but is a chapter page, not an individual profile; it separately distinguishes Secundus the Silent, a second-century Athenian philosopher.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: No target-specific person page found; the philosopher is a different person.

entries.recommendationJa: Targeted search performed; the chapter list and unrelated philosopher are not suitable biography links.

wikipediaPagesChecked.title: Search for School of Tyrannus/Tyrannus
wikipediaPagesChecked.checked: Targeted Wikipedia-domain search for “School of Tyrannus” and Acts 19:9 did not surface an article about the hall or named eponym. The returned non-Wikipedia sites were modern organizations or commentary and are not Wikipedia pages. Existing person_3 research found the bare Tyrannus target redirected to an unrelated bird article.
wikipediaPagesChecked.decision: No target-specific Wikipedia page found; this profile treats Tyrannus as an unidentified eponym and not a known person.

entries.recommendationJa: Targeted search performed; no appropriate article. Do not link the unrelated bare-title page or non-Wikipedia sites.

noteJa: この監査はプロフィール草稿・evidence・catalogを編集していない。推薦は候補として親に報告するだけであり、Wikipediaリンクを追加したことを意味しない。
languageSearchNoteJa: 対象名と初出箇所の日本語クエリでも検索し、日本語記事が見つかった場合は本文を確認する方針で調べた。今回、適合する日本語専用記事は確認できなかった。候補記事は英語またはドイツ語で、言語の違いも各レコードに反映した。
